nodes.name: Electrochemical lithiation at 0.75 V
nodes.procedure: NiCo₂O₄ nanorods underwent electrochemical lithiation tuning through intercalation and two-step conversion reaction at cut-off voltage of 0.75 V (1.07-0.35 V conversion range), followed by removal of Li₂O by water treatment.

unit_operations.name: Intercalation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Early in the lithiation process, Li⁺ ions are inserted into 16c site

unit_operations.name: Conversion reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: compound is then converted into rock-salt phase NiO, CoO, and Li₂O

unit_operations.name: Li₂O removal
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: after the removal of Li₂O by water treatment

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical lithiation processes of NiCo₂O₄ shown in Figure 1a undergo an intercalation and two-step conversion reaction mechanism... The NiCo₂O₄ nanorods at different lithiation voltages were characterized after the removal of Li₂O by water treatment.

nodes.name: Annealing to remove defects
nodes.procedure: Li-0.75 V samples were annealed at 350 °C for 1 h to remove the generated defects.
nodes.source_text: we prepared Li-0.75 V-350 °C samples by annealing the Li-0.75 V samples at 350°C for 1h to remove the generated defects.

nodes.name: NiO nanosheet synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiO nanosheets were prepared by adjusting the synthesis parameters.
nodes.source_text: we prepared NiO nanosheets and CoO nanorods by adjusting the synthesis parameters (Figure S2a,b, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: CoO nanorod synthesis
nodes.procedure: CoO nanorods were prepared by adjusting the synthesis parameters.
nodes.source_text: we prepared NiO nanosheets and CoO nanorods by adjusting the synthesis parameters (Figure S2a,b, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: CoO@NiO mixing synthesis
nodes.procedure: CoO@NiO sample was synthesized by mixing pure NiO and CoO according to the Co and Ni atomic ratio of Li-0.75 V.
nodes.source_text: CoO@NiO sample was synthesized by mixing pure NiO and CoO according to the Co and Ni atomic ratio of Li-0.75 V (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diameter of NiCo₂O₄ nanorods is about 100 nm; Li-0.75 V shows 25% radial expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a,b displays that the diameter of the synthesized nanorods is about 100 nm ... the expansion rate of Li-0.75V is in the range of 25% (Figure 2e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes 0.286 nm/0.244 nm corresponding to (220)/(311) planes of spinel NiCo₂O₄; Li-0.75 V shows bent/discontinuous lattice stripes and transformation to 2-5 nm interconnected nanoparticles from original 10-50 nm particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c, the lattice stripe of the nanorods is 0.286 nm/0.244 nm which corresponds to the (220)/(311) plane of spinel NiCo₂O₄ ... NiCo₂O₄ with original nanoparticles of 10-50 nm is transformed into interconnected nanoparticles of 2-5 nm in size after lithiation to 0.75 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of NiCo₂O₄ shows polycrystalline diffraction rings of spinel phase; Li-0.75 V shows rings attributed to rock-salt NiO and CoO phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is further supported by the selected area electron diffraction pattern of the reference nanorods, which shows the polycrystalline diffraction rings of spinel NiCo₂O₄ (Figure 2d). However, the diffraction rings displayed by Li-0.75 V are attributed to the rock-salt phase NiO and CoO (Figure 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows all expected elements (Ni, Co, O) clearly distinguished in both NiCo₂O₄ and Li-0.75 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mapping tests of NiCo₂O₄ (Figure 2i) and Li-0.75 V (Figure 2j) show that all expected elements can be clearly distinguished.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of NiCo₂O₄ shows cubic spinel phase (JCPDS No. 73-1702); Li-0.75 V shows rock-salt NiO (JCPDS No. 47-1049) and CoO (JCPDS No. 42-1300) phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S3, Supporting Information, the XRD pattern of the NiCo₂O₄ shows characteristic peaks which can be assigned to the cubic phase NiCo₂O₄ (JCPDS No. 73-1702)... For the Li-0.75 V sample, the characteristic peaks can be attributed to the rock-salt phases NiO (JCPDS No. 47-1049) and CoO (JCPDS No. 42-1300).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows 73% oxygen defects in Li-0.75 V; Co 2p₃/₂ shows 1.2 eV shift to higher binding energy and Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio of 2.44; Ni 2p₃/₂ shows decreased Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio indicating lower oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the relatively high content of oxygen defects in Li-0.75 V (73%) ... an extremely large shift of about 1.2 eV of the Co2p 3/2 peak toward higher binding energy ... The intensity ratio of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ in Li-0.75 V (2.44) ... the intensity ratio of Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ in Li-0.75 V decreases.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strong signal peak at g = 2.002 in Li-0.75 V, confirming oxygen defects formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A strong signal peak at g = 2.002 was found in Li-0.75 V, which confirms the formation of oxygen defects after lithiation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Band gap of Li-0.75 V becomes narrower after lithiation compared to NiCo₂O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the fitted optical Eg, the Eg of the Li-0.75 V becomes narrower after lithiation.

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl = 76.2 mF cm⁻² for Li-0.75 V calculated from CVs at different scan rates, indicating highest electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: C_dl is calculated from cyclic voltammogram with different scan rates in Figure S8 ... Li-0.75 V shows the highest C_dl (76.2 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Li-0.75 V has the smallest charge transfer resistance R_ct among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Li-0.75 V is the smallest compared to other samples in Figure S16.
